recipes.name: Pepperoni Bread
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 pound) loaf frozen bread dough, thawed

steps.text: Place thawed dough into a bowl; cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Roll dough into a rectangle, then brush with beaten egg and arrange pepperoni over top. Sprinkle mozzarella, Parmesan, and Italian seasoning over pepperoni. Roll dough over fillings like a jelly roll and pinch the seam to seal. Place dough, seam-side down, onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 40 minutes.
Use a bread knife to cut loaf into slices of your desired size.

raw_recipe.headline: Pepperoni Bread
raw_recipe.description: Pizza-inspired pepperoni bread is easy to make with frozen bread dough, pepperoni, and cheese. It's like pizza toppings are rolled up in a crust!

review.reviewBody: My 6-year old loves pepperoni pizza, so I made this as a pre-birthday treat. I make my own pizza dough and had some leftover, so I used it instead of the frozen bread dough. Here's a tip to help avoid excess grease (especially if you are a pepperoni purist like me and won't use turkey pepperoni) - lay pepperoni out on a double layer of paper towels and microwave for 15 - 20 seconds, then cover with 2 more paper towels and blot. I do this when I make pizza and had very little grease when I baked my bread. Brushed with olive oil and sprinkled with a little garlic powder and kosher salt before baking. Great appetizer - I'll be making this for Super Bowl.

The dough used does make a difference as some are sweet. Pizza dough (check size bc some are enough for 2 loaves) or thawed Rhodes frozen bread dough works well. Cooking the thinly sliced pepperoni for 30-60 seconds evenly arranged on top of paper towel and with additional paper towel over top (which absorbs grease as it cooks), reduces amount of grease from the pepperoni, so bread isn’t as greasy.
Egg inside is not necessary, and putting sauce inside can make the bread soggy. I use 2 cups of mozzarella and less Italian seasoning. I also bake on parchment paper instead of greasing pan. Mine was done after 25 min. Great dipped in sauce.

I used Pillsbury Pizza crust in refrigerated section of store . Slight rolled a little thiner than how it came. Used egg wash and sprinkled garlic powder and Italian seasoning directly on dough before adding my pepperoni and cheeses. After rolling up jelly roll style, egg washed top and ends and again and more Italian seasoning on top. Served with Classico Traditional Pizza sauce for dipping. Very good!

This came out fantastic, we ended up making a 2nd one instead of a pizza. I did make a few alterations to my taste. Bought a bag of 1lb dough from Stop & Shop ($1.75 I think). Used 3/4 cup mozzarella and 3/4 cup of 2% mozzarella since I like things cheesy. I only sprinkled a bit of grated parm. My fiance laid the dough out and then covered with the egg. I heated in the microwave 6 big slices of genoa and 10-12 slices of margherita pepperoni one 2 paper towels and dabbed after. I put down 3/4 cup of mozz and some parm and a bit of seasoning, then put the meat another 3/4 cup of parm with a bit more seasoning. After we rolled it we dabbed a bit of egg along top and I sprinkled a bit of parm/mozz with some garlic along the top and baked. It was fantastic!
For an even easier version, buy Pillsbury thin pizza crust. Unroll and you're ready to top!

This came out very well. My kids (teenagers) loved it. Used Pillsbury thin pizza crust, microwaved pepperoni on paper towels first to get rid of grease and did the rest as they recommended. First time making it I didnt put any pizza sauce in it. 2nd time I did put a little bit and I prefer it without. I also prebaked the crust for a few minutes like the package recommended to try and keep the center from being mushy and it worked pretty well. Dont overcook though---it will cook. Browns golden with the egg whites brushed on!!

I had a last minute function and needed a crowd-pleaser to pass, so I chose this recipe since it appeared to be the simplest with the least amount of ingredients to purchase or dig out of my cabinet. I started with fresh pizza dough from the grocer rather than frozen due to my time constraint. Roll, twirl, repeat, easy. Then I grabbed every partial pack of cheese in my fridge and loaded it on. (white American, parmesan, mozzarella, & provolone). Then I layered it with turkey pepperoni (zero grease factor), sprinkled it with Italian seasoning, rolled it up tight, cut a few steam holes in the top, rubbed a bit of egg, then sprinkled a bit of cheese & a bit more seasoning, and popped it in the oven. Two loaves fit on a large cookie sheet with non-stick foil on the bottom to catch any oozing cheese. I also made a meat-free version with pesto sauce and cheese. I sliced it in one inch sections, wrapped in in foil, an headed to the tailgate party. Four large loaves of this pizza bread were inhaled in less than 30 minutes. This recipe is definitely a great way to use up leftovers in the fridge. I'm thinking about trying a breakfast version for trips. Anyway, best wishes...Enjoy!

This is very similar to the Pepperoni Bread I have made for years. I recommend grinding the pepperoni in a food processor rather than using the round slices (the loaf rolls easier and makes a nicer presentation when the bread is sliced). My recipe is a little bit more simple; I use the frozen bread dough but I brush the rolled dough on the inside with a minced garlic paste before the main ingredients are added and just use pepperoni and shredded provolone cheese, roll the dough lengthwise (from the long side) and brush the loaf with egg to get a nice golden, shiny finished product.

This pepperoni bread is a HUGE hit at my fiance's work Christmas party every year. They tell me I can't come unless I bring the bread! However, I will give a few suggestions (that I got from others on here) on how I make it and it is delicious. First, I use the Pillsbury French Loaf. Now, it can be a little stressful rolling it out because sometimes it gets really sticky, but I find if you keep it in the fridge until the second you are going to unroll it, it's fine (also flouring your hands helps too). I also use turkey pepperoni instead of the regular pepperoni. It doesn't make the bread greasy and it tastes just as good. Also, once it's all rolled up, I brush the egg wash on top of the dough and sprinkle it with some parmesan cheese and the bread comes out nice and golden when baked for about 20 minutes. This is the perfect way to make this pepperoni bread and it will be a hit! People will be begging you to make it for all occasions!

I made this for my family. I used fresh whole wheat pizza dough from Trader Joe's and baked it on my pizza stone.
I also brushed the egg wash on the top and sprinkled poppy seeds on top before baking. It looked very nice served with a salad and tasted great.

I thought this recipe was good. I used 1 dozen bread dough rolls, for the recipe written as is. I tested some with the seasoning, which I wasn't sure about and I decided not to use it. It was too over-powering. I always made these with just pepperoni, but I really liked the addition of both the mozzarella and parmesan. I used a finely grated parmesan instead of shredded and whole milk mozzarella. I think, it worked well. I also made some as is with the egg wash and 2 cheeses, but added little bit of of spinach on top for a vegetarian version. I baked them on parchment at 425 degrees for about 10-12 minutes.

This is a great recipe!! It gets gobbled up so quickly! I'm not sure if it's a typo, but I used the egg wash on the outside of the bread and sprinkled with seasonings and grated parmesan. We experimented with the inside seasonings as well, which is what makes it fun to make! We used, Tuscan olive oil seasoning, red chile flakes, garlic powder and Italian seasoning and we spread those directly on the dough before adding the pepperoni and cheeses. All variations were delicious! Thanks for a great recipe!! (I may try the next one using the egg wash on the inside as well to see if it makes a difference.)
Easy and absolutely delicious.Both family and friends love this when I make it and there are never any leftovers!!
Simply delicious. Made this for Super Bowl and it was a crowd pleaser. I added egg wash to top on mine to add in everything seasoning and it was perfect. Will be making this on a regular basis!!!
Very easy to make and tasty! I used the Pillsbury French Loaf so it only needed to bake for 25 minutes. Next time I will serve with marinara sauce for dipping.
love it!
So good we had it for lunch and dinner.

Was great! The whole family devoured it. 
Served Marinara on the side. 
I did add some Italian seasoning to the top of the bread which was so good.
Recipe is very easy to make, very tasty, and fun for everyone! Its definatly a keeper. Only thing I did different was made the pizza dough from scratch.
I'm not sure who liked it best, the grandkids or my husband! We had pizza sauce on the side for dipping. Yummy!
